assessments.reasoning: RFC 7405 explicitly updates RFC 5234. Its §2.1 identifies US-ASCII and gives the %s and %i modes, and concrete examples establish that an unprefixed form uses case-insensitive matching.

challenge.method: Compared the older RFC’s default and numeric literals with RFC 7405 §§2.1–2.2, rejected erratum 5334, and the IETF approval notice for subsequent Internet Standard status.
challenge.results: The numeric spelling existed before the new prefixes. The rejected §2.2 proposal would change the syntax and supplies no amendment. Later standards status is separate from the December 2014 text and the matching behavior stated there.

limitations: Limited to literal matching in the December 2014 update. No assertion covers Unicode folding, rule-name identity, or implementation compliance.
